cards.text: Adam and Eve are out of the garden now. Then Eve does something nobody in history has EVER done: she has a baby, a boy named Cain. No books, no classes, and NOBODY to call for advice.

cards.question: Holding her brand new son, Eve says she brought forth a man with the help of ___.

cards.text: Later, Eve has another son: Abel, Cain’s little brother. And the boys grow up and go to work.

cards.question: Cain and Abel each have their own line of work. What is Abel’s?
And Cain, the big brother, works the ground like his dad. He is a tiller of the ___.

cards.text: In the course of time, the brothers bring offerings to the LORD. Cain the farmer brings some of the fruit of the soil.

cards.question: Abel is the shepherd. What does Abel bring to the LORD as his offering?

answers.text: The best of the firstborn of his flock
A basket of grain from the fields
A pair of doves from the nearby hills

cards.question: Both brothers have brought their offerings to the LORD. True or false: The LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering.
But the LORD has no regard for Cain and his offering. How does Cain take it?

cards.text: Cain’s countenance falls too. Then the LORD Himself asks him, “Why are you angry, and why has your countenance fallen?”

cards.question: The LORD tells Cain that if he does what is right he will be accepted. But if he refuses, something is crouching at his door. What is it?
Sin desires Cain, but the LORD tells Cain he must ___ it.

cards.text: With that warning still hanging in the air, Cain goes and speaks to his brother Abel.

cards.question: True or false: Cain asks his brother Abel to go out to the field with him.

cards.text: And while the two of them are out in the field, Cain rises up against his brother Abel and kills him.
Abel is gone. Then the LORD comes to Cain with a question: “Where is your brother Abel?”

cards.question: True or false: When the LORD asks Cain where Abel is, Cain answers that he does not know.

cards.text: Then Cain adds, “Am I my brother’s keeper?” Friend, I KNOW that move, because I have stood next to an empty cookie box with crumbs in my mustache going, "Cookies? What cookies?"

cards.question: The LORD answers Cain, “What have you done?” Then He says something is crying out to Him from the ground. What is it?

cards.text: Now Cain is cursed and banished from the ground. That’s the same ground that opened its mouth to receive his brother’s blood from his hand.

cards.question: Cain the farmer is banished from the ground. True or false: When Cain tills the ground from now on, it will still yield its produce to him.
The ground won’t yield to Cain anymore. So what does the LORD say Cain will be on the earth?

cards.text: Then Cain says to the LORD, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.”

cards.question: Cain says he is driven from the face of the earth and will be hidden from the LORD’s face. What does Cain say will happen to him out there?

answers.text: Whoever finds him will kill him
The ground will swallow him up
Wild beasts will hunt him down

cards.text: And the LORD replies, “Not so!” Then He makes a promise about anyone who slays Cain.

cards.question: The LORD says that if anyone slays Cain, then Cain will be avenged ___.
What does the LORD place on Cain so that no one who finds him will kill him?

cards.text: So Cain goes out from the presence of the LORD.

cards.question: Cain settles down east of Eden. In what land?

cards.text: Out in Nod, Cain and his wife have a son named Enoch. And Cain gets busy building.

cards.question: Cain builds a ___ and names it after his son Enoch.

cards.text: From Enoch, the family line runs down to Lamech, who marries two women, Adah and Zillah. Their sons start whole new kinds of work: Jabal with tents and livestock, Jubal with the harp and flute, and Tubal-cain forging bronze and iron. Tubal-cain has a sister too, Naamah. One family, and they’ve got housing, music AND hardware covered.
Then Lamech calls his wives together, and he opens BIG: “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my speech.”

cards.question: What does Lamech tell Adah and Zillah he has done?

answers.text: Slain a man for wounding him
Forgiven a man for striking him
Built a new city for his sons

cards.question: Lamech brings up how Cain is avenged sevenfold, and then he tries to top it. How much does Lamech say he will be avenged?

cards.text: Back to Adam and Eve. They have another son, and Eve names him Seth.

cards.question: Eve says God has granted her another seed in place of ___, since Cain killed him.

cards.text: Seth grows up and has a son of his own, and he calls him Enosh.

cards.question: True or false: At that time, men began to call upon the name of the LORD.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "Why are you angry, and why has your countenance fallen?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Adam and Eve are out of the garden now. That fact comes from Genesis 3:23-24, but the card cites only Genesis 4:1 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke says Eve had NOBODY to call for advice. In the next card, and in Genesis 4:1, Eve says she brought forth a man with the help of the LORD. The joke works against what the text says and against the answer to card 2.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The question says Cain works the ground, then asks him to fill in 'a tiller of the ___'. That gives away 'soil' and rules out 'forest' and 'wilderness'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Like his dad' draws on Adam working the ground in Genesis 3:23, which is outside the passage. The card cites only Genesis 4:2 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card says the brothers bring offerings, so it includes Abel bringing one, which is Genesis 4:4. It cites only Genesis 4:3.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The comparison ('Cookies? What cookies?') is playing dumb, which matches 'I do not know!'. But it is attached to 'Am I my brother's keeper?', which pushes off responsibility. The everyday action doesn't match the line it rides on.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 5 of the 8 choice cards in this stop (cards 4, 7, 9, 12, 14). True or false has 2 and fill in the blank has only 1.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: 'So what does the LORD say Cain will be' makes being a fugitive and a wanderer the result of the ground not yielding. Genesis 4:12 gives the two statements side by side without saying how they connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card calls the LORD's words a 'promise'. Genesis 4:15 doesn't call them that. It just says what the LORD replied.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card says Lamech's sons 'start whole new kinds of work'. Abel already kept sheep in Genesis 4:2, so raising livestock isn't new. Also, Tubal-cain is called only 'a forger of every implement of bronze and iron', not the father of forgers (4:22). The card stretches the text and says something the text shows isn't so.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'Lamech brings up how Cain is avenged sevenfold' drops the 'If' in Lamech's line, 'If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold' (4:24).
The question includes 'since Cain killed him', which makes Abel the only answer that makes sense. 'In place of Cain, since Cain killed him' doesn't work, and Enoch is Cain's own son.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card sets up calling on the name of the LORD, and 'At that time' doesn't say which time (the days of Seth and Enosh). The baker can only guess on a coin flip.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin has almost no comic voice. The whole walkthrough has about four joke moments (stop 1 card 1, stop 2 card 3, stop 3 cards 3 and 4). Many story cards are bare retellings with no personality, including stop 1 cards 3, 6 and 13, stop 2 cards 8 and 13, and stop 3 cards 7 and 9. Moments that could easily hold a laugh go unused, like Lamech's big boast.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
